items.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
items.q: He taught Joe. He taught Joe. He taught Joe. ... And that's how he learned how to play the string instrument, you see.

ctx.x: And you knew that Joe Oliver did. Yeah.

Well, I just laughed and talked about Joe. We were just talking about Joe. And some of them boys, you know, he taught. Did you say he taught Joe Oliver? He taught Joe. He taught Joe. And many times, he'd give somebody else a present. I'd say, well, they never say nothing about Joe, Steve and Joe. And I know that. He taught Joe and Joe played in his brass band. And when he got the string band, as they call in those days, and used to play out of the lake for all the country clubs and all the places out of the lake.…
We talked to Mrs. Oliver, Joe Oliver's wife, Mrs. Stella Oliver. Yeah. She couldn't remember the name of his teacher.

items.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
items.q: He made a name for himself when he left. When he left here.

ctx.x: And so many things they did.
See, Joe Oliver or King Oliver as they call him, he made the first really important record.
When he went away from here, you see. He made a name for himself when he left. When he left here.
